# Beyond discount rates: A valuation framework for unpriced systematic risk

> Code and data behind the empirical exhibits of an article that splits an asset's expected return
> into a cost of capital and a gain of capital, the part that comes from misjudged future cash
> flows. For three US equity index funds (SPY, QQQ, IWM), 2000 to 2023, it holds the cost of
> capital of each and the realized and implied gain of capital at four horizons. The article's text
> is the publisher's and is not included.

Replication package by Agisilaos Papadogiannis (https://github.com/apapadogiannis).
Forthcoming in The Journal of Investing (2027). Preprint: https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5180040
Code and data: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/beyond-discount-rates  Archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24243060
Version 1.1.0, released 2026-11-21. A package is a fixed record: it changes only by a new
release, and a release that changes a reported number gets a new major version.
This file is written for AI agents and other programs. People should start at the README.

## Coverage

- Exhibit 10: the annual cost of capital of SPY, QQQ and IWM, the geometric mean return of each
  over its own sample.
- Exhibit 11: the realized gain of capital at horizons of 6, 12, 24 and 36 months, for every start
  month, with summary statistics by fund and horizon.
- Equation 21 and Proposition 6: the implied gain of capital and its exact proportionality to the
  realized gain, checked on every observation.
- A numerical check of the article's closed-form results on 100,000 random parameter draws
  (scripts/check_identities.py).
- Exhibits 1 to 3 and 7 to 9 of the article are tables and a flow diagram and have no code or data
  here.

## What this adds over reading the paper or recomputing

1. The price file is stored as downloaded. Yahoo rescales its adjusted prices after every
   distribution, so a later download gives different levels and, through rounding, slightly
   different returns. The article's numbers are those of this file.
2. The definitions are fixed and stated: with month-end prices P, an annual cost of capital c and a
   horizon of h months, C = (1+c)^(h/12); realized gain = P_T/P_t - C; implied gain = realized gain
   / C. The cost of capital of a fund is its own geometric mean return over the sample.
3. outputs/gain_of_capital.csv gives both gains for every fund, horizon and start month, so any
   statistic of the article can be recomputed from the series and not only read from the summary.
4. The results are stored as they were when the paper's numbers were taken from them. A check
   reruns the code on the stored data and compares every stored result file with the fresh one,
   number by number (relative tolerance 1e-9; text and whole numbers exactly). It runs on every
   change and once a month, and the badge in the README shows the last run.

## Fields of outputs/results.json

- `sample`: first and last month-end price used, and the horizons in months
- `exhibit10_cost_of_capital`: by fund: the index it tracks, its own first and last month,
  `months`, and `cost_of_capital_pct`, its geometric mean annual return over that sample, in per
  cent
- `exhibit11_realized_gain`: by horizon (6m, 12m, 24m, 36m), then by fund: `observations`, the
  number of start months; `first_start_month`, `last_start_month`; `mean`, `std`, `min`, `max` of
  the realized gain, as fractions, with the start months of the minimum and maximum;
  `share_abs_above_20pp`, the share of start months with a gain above 0.20 in absolute value;
  `share_positive`, overall and for start months in 2000 to 2002 and in 2010 to 2018;
  `autocorrelation_lag1`; `sign_changes`, the number of times the gain changes sign from one start
  month to the next. Each horizon also has `dispersion`, the standard deviation of QQQ and of IWM
  over that of SPY
- `proposition6_proportionality`: `observations`, the number of fund, horizon and start-month cases
  checked; `max_abs_deviation_below_1e-12`, true if implied gain equals realized gain divided by
  the compounded cost of capital in every case; `implied_over_realized`, that ratio by fund and
  horizon

## Files

- outputs/results.json: every number behind Exhibits 10 and 11 and the statements made about them,
  under keys named after the exhibits: `sample`, `exhibit10_cost_of_capital` (by fund),
  `exhibit11_realized_gain` (by horizon, then by fund, with a `dispersion` entry per horizon),
  `proposition6_proportionality`. It holds 163 numbers, and under `package` the paper, the
  identifiers, the version, the licence and the citation. Start here.
- outputs/gain_of_capital.csv: columns date (the start month), ticker, horizon_months, g_realized,
  g_implied.
- data/etf_adjclose_monthly.csv: the prices. data/README.md gives source, retrieval date and terms.
  The row dated the first of a month holds the adjusted close at the end of that month.
- paper/abstract.pdf: the title and abstract of the article. The full text is at the publisher.

Raw files: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/beyond-discount-rates/main/<path>, for example https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/beyond-discount-rates/main/outputs/results.json

## How to read the figures

- Units: `cost_of_capital_pct` is in per cent a year. Every gain of capital (mean, std, min, max,
  and the two columns of gain_of_capital.csv) is a fraction of the starting price over the whole
  horizon: 0.05 is 5 percentage points. Shares, autocorrelations and ratios are plain numbers.
- A start month such as 2008-02 means the price at the end of that month. `months` in Exhibit 10 is
  the number of monthly returns, one less than the number of month-end prices.
- `std` is the sample standard deviation. `autocorrelation_lag1` is between a gain and the gain
  that starts one month later, on the overlapping series. The package gives no count of independent
  observations; the number of non-overlapping windows is the observations divided by the horizon in
  months.
- A realized gain can be below -1: it is the price ratio less the compounded cost of capital, so a
  large loss over a long horizon gives, for example, -1.003.
- The proportionality of the implied to the realized gain is exact in the computation. In
  gain_of_capital.csv both are rounded to six decimals, so their ratio there matches only to about
  four decimals.
- The gain of capital is defined against the fund's own average return over the same sample. Its
  mean is therefore close to zero by construction; the article's findings are about its size,
  persistence and sign regimes, not its average.
- A gain is dated by its start month and covers the following h months. `last_start_month` is
  therefore earlier than the end of the sample by the horizon.
- Gains are over the whole horizon and are not annualised. A 36-month gain and a 6-month gain are
  not on the same scale.
- `share_abs_above_20pp` is the share of start months in which the gain exceeds 20 percentage
  points in absolute value. `dispersion` is the standard deviation of QQQ or IWM over that of SPY
  at the same horizon.
- Observations at one horizon overlap, so they are strongly autocorrelated and are not independent
  draws.
- IWM starts in May 2000, so its sample is shorter than that of SPY and QQQ.

## Do not use this for

- A forecast of returns, or a signal to buy or sell. The realized gain is known only after the
  horizon has passed.
- Anything after December 2023. The package is a fixed record and is not updated.
- The cost of capital of these funds in general. The figure here is the sample's own average
  return, used as the benchmark the gain is measured against.
- The article's argument or wording. This package holds its numbers, not its text.

The results in outputs/ are released under CC BY 4.0

The prices are monthly adjusted closing prices from Yahoo Finance. They remain the property of
their source, are included for replication with attribution, and are not covered by the licence
above.
